component.name: Synergy
component.summary: Share one keyboard and mouse between computers

description.p: Use the keyboard, mouse, or trackpad of one computer to control nearby computers, and work seamlessly between them.

A security and Wayland release. It closes four advisories, makes hotkeys and the cursor behave on a Wayland server, and repairs upgrading from 1.20 or older, which could arrive with the settings, the serial key and the log level reset. Highlights since the previous release:

ul.li: CVE-2026-63409: an odd-length DSOP options vector caused an out-of-bounds read in the client.
CVE-2026-65832: an unauthenticated, server-controlled out-of-bounds read in modifier-table indexing.
CVE-2026-65976: a clipboard receiver could accumulate data beyond the configured clipboard size limit.
GHSA-vxgx-6p4m-fv83: a single-byte LSYN language payload caused an uncaught exception in the client.
Further memory-safety hardening in clipboard handling.
Hotkeys now work on a Wayland server, through the GlobalShortcuts portal, and the portal permission prompt no longer reappears on every start, after sleep, or when the display wakes.
Many cursor fixes on Wayland, covering multi-monitor edges, input capture that never engaged, screen switches during a drag, and the cursor jumping when the compositor renegotiates input devices.
Scroll wheels that send small deltas are no longer ignored.
Keyboard fixes for the numpad on Wayland, keys left stuck on an X11 client when its keyboard map refreshes, and modifier keys left stuck after crossing screens.
Administrators can apply a locked settings file at launch again.
Settings, the serial key and the log level now survive an upgrade from 1.20 or older.
The Flatpak build no longer reports itself as a beta development build.
Various macOS and Windows fixes and improvements.

description.p: See the release notes for the full changelog.
A maintenance release for the 1.21 line, whose main addition is clipboard sharing on Wayland. Highlights since the previous release:

ul.li: Clipboard sharing now works on Wayland, using the desktop portals.
The version shown in the interface no longer repeats the commit hash.

description.p: See the release notes for the full changelog.
This release folds a large number of upstream improvements into Synergy from Deskflow, much of it built by the Synergy team and contributed upstream. Highlights since the previous release:

ul.li: CVE-2021-42072: the client's identity was not sufficiently verified when it connected.
CVE-2021-42073: an attacker could enter an active session state.
CVE-2021-42074: an attacker could cause a segmentation fault in the server component.
CVE-2021-42075: the server did not correctly close file descriptors for established TCP connections.
CVE-2021-42076: an attacker could exhaust memory in the server and client components by sending long TCP messages.
TLS fingerprints are now kept in a fingerprint database, with a clearer comparison dialog that shows both the local and remote prints side by side.
A new option for servers to require a client certificate before accepting a connection.
The app now connects to the running core process over a dedicated IPC channel and receives status updates directly, instead of inferring the connection state by parsing log output.
Only one copy of the core runs at a time, so duplicate instances no longer fight over the connection.
On Windows, clipboard changes are tracked with a modern format-listener API for more reliable clipboard sharing.
A single combined core binary replaces the separate client and server processes.
A hotkey to cycle through computers, and an option to start with the cursor locked to the current computer.
An option to show the version in the window title.
The server address can be a list of host names or IP addresses, with a more accurate suggested address that updates as the network changes.
A new client configuration dialog, a searchable log you can dock and hide, millisecond timestamps, and a refreshed about dialog and status area.
A setting to choose the network protocol (Synergy or Barrier) for compatibility with different clients.
Live interface translation without restarting, with Spanish, Italian, Japanese, Chinese (simplified), Korean, and Russian added.
Mono or colorful tray icons with matching light and dark icon themes.
A new scroll scaling option replaces the old scroll-speed setting.
On Linux, server and client configuration honors XDG_CONFIG_HOME.
